content: Section 14.10 of the American Diabetes Association (ADA) guidelines has been revised to emphasize the importance of screening for psychosocial and behavioral health concerns in patients. It also highlights the necessity of making appropriate referrals to address these issues effectively. Section 53 has been updated to recommend a weight loss goal of 7-10% for youth diagnosed with type 2 diabetes, as part of their management plan. Section 70 now advises considering the use of empagliflozin prior to intensifying insulin therapy in children with type 2 diabetes, to optimize treatment outcomes. Section 69 suggests evaluating the impact of medications on weight and considering medication adherence when managing youth with overweight or obesity and type 2 diabetes. Section 72 has replaced the term severe obesity with class 2 obesity or higher, defined as a BMI ≥ 35 kg/m² or 120% of the 95th percentile for age and sex. This change provides a more precise framework for identifying adolescents who may be candidates for metabolic surgery. Section 78 has been updated to provide clearer guidance on protein intake recommendations for children with nephropathy, tailored to their age. Section 107 strongly discourages the initiation of smoking, including both tobacco and e-cigarettes, in youth with diabetes. It also emphasizes the importance of smoking cessation and educates on the harmful effects of smoking and exposure to secondhand smoke in this population. The section on the transition from pediatric to adult care has been revised to underscore the critical role of interprofessional teams in facilitating this process. It stresses the importance of coordinated care between pediatric specialists and caregivers to determine the appropriate timing for transitioning to adult care.
